source.title: Dropout Universality: Scaling Laws and Optimal Scheduling at the Edge-of-Chaos

record.tranche_reason: Reports training-accuracy curves for CIFAR-10 MLPs trained from initialization, a different architecture from the convolutional networks named in V1.
record.gate_note: The paper’s main experiments compare dropout schedules and report test performance. CIFAR-10 MLP training-accuracy outcomes appear only in figures; text does not state their plotted values.
record.test_reason: The study uses initialization signal-propagation theory to guide dropout placement and evaluates its own schedules. It does not compare initialization-dependent training speed or trainable depth (V4). Its training-accuracy curves concern MLPs and Transformers, outside V1's convolutional-network scope, and it tests none of V2–V6's specified training effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that front-loading dropout can improve validation-selected models and restrain late test-loss increases, with more consistent gains in MLPs. Their propagation theory describes initialization and cannot alone predict trained performance.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains MLPs to compare dropout placement and generalization; it does not reproduce the claim’s convolutional-network training-error recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Dropout schedule and strength vary across the plotted training-accuracy curves.

fits_no_version.finding: Training-accuracy trajectories are plotted for CIFAR-10 MLP dropout schedules; numerical outcomes are unavailable in the supplied text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout placement affects training trajectories in six-hidden-layer CIFAR-10 MLPs.

fits_no_version.finding: The theory derives activation-dependent correlation-length scaling at initialization and motivates concentrating dropout near the input.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout strength and activation regularity determine initialization correlation propagation under the stated mean-field assumptions.

fits_no_version.finding: Front-loaded dropout improves test performance in several settings, with more consistent gains in MLPs; some Transformer comparisons are inconclusive.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Redistributing dropout toward early layers can improve generalization and reduce late test-loss increases.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: The relevant training-accuracy outcomes are figure-only and not described numerically in text; the experiments use MLPs rather than the convolutional networks specified by V1.

untested.parts: Convolutional-network training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and the stated size, stopping and regularization qualifications.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization failures and their reduction through extra student neurons.
Depth-related training degradation and prevention through identity shortcuts or the specified alternative recipes.
Effects of initialization choices on learning speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization. Initialization correlation lengths alone do not measure these outcomes.
Loss recovery, curvature changes and divergence relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: No claim-version verdict is warranted. Figure-only values remain undetermined; test accuracy and initialization correlation length cannot substitute for the training effects named by the versions.

versions.untested_parts: The plotted CIFAR-10 MLP training-accuracy curves do not test V1’s convolutional-network conditions or its claims about corrupted or random labels, smaller models, early stopping, or substantial residual training error.
